title: Merge Hypothesis Ledger — PR forensics + small-change safety
content:
Purpose / context:
- Capture quick hypotheses and small-change safety patterns for high-risk PRs that touch runtime/kvcache/batching. This is a personal ledger I keep while triaging and writing small fixes. Treat as working notes.

High-level goal:
- Keep merges simple and reversible while preserving latency SLOs. For any PR that changes request routing, caching, or batching: prefer feature flags, explicit rollbacks, and a minimal canary matrix.

Immediate checklist (run before merge):
- [ ] Add a scoped feature flag (ff: pr-<id>-safe) with default OFF in config layer.
- [ ] Add a short rollout plan to PR description (canary percentage/time).
- [ ] Add token-level and route-level logging gated behind ff for 48h.
- [ ] Add a smoke test that asserts: median latency <= baseline + 10ms and no new 5xx in canary window.
- [ ] Confirm MKS/ops are informed (ping #infra on canary start).

Quick forensics template (if regressions appear post-merge):
1) What changed? (files / modules)
   - note imports, new opt-in flags, kernel selection logic.
2) Symptoms: latency increase? error codes? evictions?
3) Repro steps (local / staging): exact docker/commit and request patterns.
4) Hypotheses (ranked): small, testable bullets.
5) Mitigations tested: revert, ff toggle, config tweak.
6) Outcome and next actions.

Example hypotheses I write often:
- New batching heuristic increases average batch depth for short sequences -> increases tail latency.
- KV cache invalidation condition too aggressive after model-version header change -> higher compute per request.
- Kernel selection fallback triggers less-optimal path for 8k seqs because sequence length bucket mis-specified.

Quick mitigations (fast-turnaround):
- Flip feature flag off (fastest).
- Revert the commit with a tiny revert PR and fast-merge.
- Patch config: tighten batch size ceiling or lower batching timeout by 5-10ms.
- Force kernel selection override to previous behavior via env var.

Small-change rollback playbook (commander commands):
- Identify offending commit: git log --oneline --graph --decorate origin/main..HEAD
- Create revert branch: git checkout -b revert/pr-<id>-<short-reason> && git revert <sha> -m 1
- Push and open revert PR, tag @oncall and @release-lead in PR description
- If revert not possible (hotfix needed), patch config in place and toggle ff

Canary matrix (my minimal default):
- Phase A (15m): 1% traffic, verify P95/median vs baseline, check 5xx
- Phase B (2h): 10% traffic, monitor cost per token and saturation metrics
- Phase C (24h): 50% traffic if A/B stable, run scheduled evals on sample prompts

Metrics to watch (and quick alert thresholds I scribble):
- median_latency_route_{X} baseline + 10ms (warn), +30ms (critical)
- p95_latency baseline + 25ms (warn)
- 5xx rate increase > 0.1% absolute
- batch_depth_mean increase > 15%
- kv_cache_hit_rate drop > 3%

Notes on tests and deterministic repro:
- Use the canned load generator (scripts/repro/generate_short_seq.sh) with the same model and quantization setting.
- For KV cache issues, reproduce with long-lived sessions to exercise prefix cache hits (simulate 10k repeated prefixes).
- When changing kernel selection, run quick perf harness: cargo run --bin perf-harness -- --model x --seq 2048 --rep 1000 and compare tail latency.

Review heuristics I try to keep in mind:
- Smaller surface > larger change: split PRs if touching routing + kernels + config.
- If PR touches both serving runtime and console (observability), file two PRs: runtime-only with ff, console-only for dashboards.
- Prefer changing defaults in config via feature flag rather than codepaths for immediate reversibility.

Follow-ups / low-priority ideas (capture here so they don't get lost):
- Auto-generate a sparse canary report in PR checks that computes simple deltas (p50/p95/5xx) against latest main in CI for a 1-minute synthetic run.
- Add a small lint in pre-commit that warns if a PR modifies kernel-selection heuristics without an associated perf test.
- Build a tiny dashboard for "active feature flags by PR" showing which PR enabled flags are live and their canary progress.

Open questions to ask on PR thread (copy-paste friendly):
- Can you add a brief perf summary for typical small and long sequence workloads? (p50/p95/cost per token)
- Is the change covered by a unit/perf test we can run in CI quickly? If not, can we add a micro-perf harness?
- Which feature flag will guard this in prod and who owns it for rollbacks?

Personal quick log (actions I have taken on this PR):
- 2025-01-12: Local perf shows +18ms p95 for short sequences on top commit. Hypothesis: batching timeout change.
- 2025-01-13: Opened a minimal revert for batching tweak and added ff.
- 2025-01-14: Canary at 1% for 30m, 5xx stable, but batch_depth_mean +12% (monitor).
- 2025-01-18: Rolled back the revert, added config limit on max_batch_depth and scheduled extended canary.

Random TODOs (one-liners):
- Write short howto for toggling ff in private deployments.
- Add an ops-runbook snippet for KV cache thrash diagnosis.
- Propose a small CI job that runs perf-harness with 100 short-seq requests and fails if p95 regresses > 20ms.

Slack copy for quick ping when starting a canary: 
"Starting canary for PR #4821 (ff:pr-4821-safe) — phase A 1% for 15m. PT: Imani. Watch: p50/p95/5xx. Link: <PR link>"

End of ledger entry 02.18.2025 — will clean up and promote any stable items to a team checklist once repeated patterns emerge.
